partner_context.their_ambition: You are Voi — Europe's leading shared micromobility operator, running ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries on a city-partnership model, profitably. You won the street layer city by city, tender by tender, on an operations-first, city-partnership model.
partner_context.their_pressure: Micromobility margins are won on utilization and city relationships — and the next differentiated surface is scarce. Streets are contested; the water in front of those same cities is empty. Every waterfront city you serve moves millions across bays, straits and archipelagos on slow diesel hulls, none of it in your app.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier gives Voi the water tier: a software-defined foiling fleet operating pier-to-pier in the cities Voi already serves — the same city-partnership playbook, extended to the harbour. Street fleet feeds pier; pier feeds street fleet.

hero.title: Voi × Navier — from the street layer to the water layer
hero.subtitle: Voi runs the streets of 130+ European cities. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Voi-integrated foiling water tier across Voi's waterfront markets. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Voi brings the app, the riders, the city relationships and a street fleet at every pier. Together we make the water crossing one more leg of the journey Voi already serves.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives — and the waterfront cities Voi serves still move by slow diesel ferry or not at all.

network_thesis.headline: Voi owns the street layer of Europe's waterfront cities. The water layer is next.
network_thesis.body: Voi — Europe's leading shared micromobility operator, running ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries on a city-partnership model, profitably. Its riders start and end their days in exactly the places Navier serves — marina districts, corniches, island quays, archipelago piers. A Navier foiling tier extends the same app from the street to the water: silent, all-electric, zero-wake crossings booked in the Voi app, with a Voi vehicle waiting at both piers.

network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a real, ready market. Start with the flagship — or pick any cluster; the phased sequence is our recommended path, not the only one.
network_thesis.coverage_note: Beyond the five proposed markets, Voi's footprint covers waterfront cities across Norway, Denmark, Germany, Switzerland, the UK, Belgium, the Netherlands and Austria — each a natural extension as corridors are mapped.

multimodal_fit: Voi's e-scooters and e-bikes already serve the streets on both sides of every crossing. The pier becomes another node in the same app: ride a Voi scooter to the quay, fly the crossing, pick up a Voi e-bike on the far side. No other operator can stage the first and last hundred metres of a water journey the way Voi can.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance & certification path, and a uniform integration spec (deep links, live seat inventory, pier locations).
the_ask.partner_brings: The app and rider base, city relationships and tender track record, and street-fleet staging at every pier — starting with the flagship market to prove the tier.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a Phase-1 pilot on the flagship market's shortest, densest crossings, building out the network as berth agreements land.

close.title: The water layer of Voi's cities.
close.body: Voi won Europe's streets city by city, in partnership with the cities themselves. The water between those cities is the next tender — same app, same rider, same partnership model.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the marinas and piers already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 sold out), decarbonization mandates turned diesel fleets into liabilities, and the hybrid removed the range excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.headline: The water layer of Voi's waterfront cities.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every water-bound market in the Voi footprint — the Greek islands, the Dalmatian coast, the Italian Riviera and lagoon, the Côte d'Azur, the UAE, Saudi's commercial Corniche, the Tagus estuary, Dublin Bay, Tallinn and the Gulf of Finland, Cyprus's south coast, the Stockholm archipelago, the Balearics and Costa Brava, the Romanian Black Sea, Helsinki, plus sovereign-data-only Israel and held Lebanon — wherever Voi demand meets the coastline.
end_state.scale: 17 markets · 27+ anchor regions · steady-state ceiling tracked in partner sheet
end_state.narrative: Steady state is a Voi water tier spanning the Mediterranean, the Atlantic edge, the Baltic and the Gulf: book a foiling vessel the same way you book a car, from Athens to Dubai to Lisbon to Tallinn.

objections.concern: Ground ride-hail is our core — why move onto water?
objections.response: Water is the one urban surface Voi's mission of cheaper, cleaner, car-free mobility hasn't reached. Across the Saronic, the Dalmatian coast and the Gulf, the sea is the fastest line between two points — and no super-app owns it yet.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for the Mediterranean and Gulf?
objections.response: Most coastal and island hops are short — inside the all-electric Pioneer II's 70 nm envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer island and cross-gulf legs up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: We operate in 45+ countries — how do we launch without huge overhead?
objections.response: You don't build or run the fleet. Navier brings vessels, captains and maintenance; Voi brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand. Each coastal city is a self-contained pilot on existing berths — no new infrastructure.

objections.concern: Will a water tier fit Voi's value positioning?
objections.response: Foiling's low energy per passenger-mile is exactly what makes an affordable water option viable. It's cleaner and car-free — on-brand for Voi — and the resort corridors fund the launch while commuters get a faster crossing.

objections.concern: You run scooters, not boats.
objections.response: So did no one, until now — the operating model is the same one you've mastered: dense urban fleets, app dispatch, city tenders, utilization economics. Navier supplies the hulls, captains and certification; you supply the city.

markets.label: Finland — Helsinki & Gulf of Finland
markets.summary: Helsinki sits on an archipelago: the city's islands — Suomenlinna, Lonna, Pihlajasaari, Korkeasaari — and the fast-growing Laajasalo/Kruunuvuorenranta waterfront are all short hops from the market square, served today by slow diesel ferries.

hero.title: Voi × Navier — Helsinki's archipelago shuttle
hero.subtitle: Foil to Suomenlinna and the islands at commuter speed, booked in the Voi app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Voi-branded electric-foiling tier across Helsinki's inner archipelago and the Laajasalo waterfront, replacing slow diesel ferries on the city's busiest short-water commutes and tourist runs.

markets.why_now: Helsinki's archipelago carries millions of ferry trips a year — Suomenlinna alone draws ~1M+ visitors — on diesel ferries that are slow and timetable-bound. The new Kruunuvuorenranta/Laajasalo district is adding waterfront commuters. Pioneer II is commercial now and every inner-archipelago leg is well under its range.
markets.multimodal_fit: Voi's e-scooters and e-bikes already serve the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Voi — Europe's leading shared micromobility operator, running ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries on a city-partnership model, profitably. Voi runs the streets of 130+ European cities — including the cities around Helsinki's archipelago waterfront. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Voi app.

why_navier_now.narrative: Every Helsinki leg is tiny by water (Suomenlinna 1.5nm, Laajasalo 2nm), squarely inside Pioneer II's commercial envelope. The Helsinki–Tallinn crossing (43nm) is also within Pioneer range, making the Gulf-of-Finland link a real near-term corridor rather than a roadmap aspiration.

markets.differentiation: Against the diesel ferry: faster, quiet, all-electric and on-demand rather than fixed-timetable. Against the road: there is no road — the water is the only direct path, and we make it fast.

proof_points.claim: Voi is Europe's leading shared micromobility operator — and profitable.
proof_points.evidence: ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries; 2025 delivered record revenue with full-year profitability and cash generation.

proof_points.claim: Helsinki's archipelago is a high-volume ferry market.
proof_points.evidence: Suomenlinna alone draws ~1M+ annual visitors; the inner islands carry millions of ferry trips a year.

proof_points.claim: The legs are short and dense.
proof_points.evidence: Market Square–Suomenlinna ~1.5nm, Helsinki–Laajasalo ~2nm — ideal Pioneer II corridors.

proof_points.claim: The Tallinn crossing is in Pioneer range.
proof_points.evidence: Helsinki–Tallinn is ~43nm, within Pioneer II's 70nm envelope — a near-term Gulf corridor, not roadmap.

proof_points.claim: Helsinki has strong decarbonization pull.
proof_points.evidence: City carbon-neutrality targets favour all-electric marine over diesel ferries.

objections.concern: Helsinki winters freeze the harbour.
objections.response: True — this is a strong shoulder/summer service. We right-size the fleet seasonally and concentrate on the high-demand ice-free months; the model assumes a seasonal, not year-round, operating window.

objections.concern: Public ferries already serve these islands cheaply.
objections.response: We don't replace the public ferry; we add a premium speed-and-frequency tier in the Voi app for riders who value time, plus the cross-Gulf Tallinn corridor the ferries serve slowly.

objections.concern: The Tallinn run sounds long for an 8-pax boat.
objections.response: It's 43nm — inside Pioneer II's 70nm range — so it's a genuine Phase-3 corridor, not a faked long leg.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a water tier with Voi across Helsinki's archipelago waterfront, starting with a small Prove fleet on the shortest, densest hops and scaling as berth agreements land — every leg booked in the Voi app.
markets.close: Helsinki is a city built on water with a million-plus ferry trips a year on diesel boats — a clean, fast, in-app foiling tier is an obvious win for Voi and for the city's climate goals.
markets.end_state: A Helsinki archipelago network plus a Pioneer-range Gulf-of-Finland link to Tallinn, all booked in the Voi app.

markets.label: France — Côte d'Azur
markets.summary: The Côte d'Azur is now modeled as a cluster of distinct premium nodes — Nice (the air gateway), Monaco, Antibes (Europe's largest yacht harbour), Cannes (Film + Yachting Festival) and St-Tropez — packed into a short, ultra-affluent coastal strip where the corniche roads jam constantly and a yacht-conditioned clientele already values water transfer. Anchor on the Cannes/Antibes yacht hubs, scale through the Nice gateway and Monaco with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run, and reach St-Tropez and the cross-border Sanremo/Portofino legs. Voi's French presence is the front door.

hero.title: Voi × Navier — Côte d'Azur
hero.subtitle: Foil the Riviera from Cannes to Monaco at speed, booked in the Voi app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Voi-branded electric-foiling tier across the Côte d'Azur cluster — Cannes, Antibes, Nice, Monaco, St-Tropez and Menton — anchored on the Cannes/Antibes yacht hubs, with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run and cross-border Sanremo/Portofino reach.

markets.why_now: The Riviera is one of the densest concentrations of wealth and yachting on earth; the corniche roads are chronically congested and the Nice Airport–Monaco helicopter/road transfer is a premium pain point. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every Riviera leg.
markets.multimodal_fit: Voi's e-scooters and e-bikes already serve the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Voi — Europe's leading shared micromobility operator, running ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries on a city-partnership model, profitably. Voi runs the streets of 130+ European cities — including the cities around the French Riviera from Cannes to Monaco. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Voi app.

why_navier_now.narrative: Every Riviera leg (Menton–Monaco 4nm, Antibes–Cannes 6nm, Nice Airport–Monaco 6.7nm, Monaco–Sanremo 13nm) is inside Pioneer II range — the whole network runs on the commercial-now hull.

markets.differentiation: Against the corniche road and the airport helicopter: comparable or better cost, faster jetty-to-jetty, with zero local emissions. Against the yacht tender: an on-demand, in-app shared premium tier.

proof_points.claim: Voi is Europe's leading shared micromobility operator — and profitable.
proof_points.evidence: ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries; 2025 delivered record revenue with full-year profitability and cash generation.

proof_points.claim: The Côte d'Azur is Europe's densest wealth-and-yachting coast.

proof_points.evidence: Menton–Monaco ~4nm, Antibes–Cannes ~6nm, Nice Airport–Monaco ~6.7nm.

objections.concern: The clientele already has yachts and helicopters.
objections.response: Exactly the point: an on-demand, in-app foiling tier is faster than the road and cheaper and greener than the helicopter, capturing the transfers between owning a yacht and queuing on the corniche.

objections.concern: Monaco has strict marine access rules.
objections.response: We operate within licensed berths and Monaco's access framework; low-wake all-electric foiling aligns with its environmental positioning.

objections.concern: The market is seasonal around events.
objections.response: Demand peaks around the Grand Prix, the film festival and summer, but year-round corporate Nice Airport–Monaco transfers provide a steady base.

markets.close: The Riviera is the world's richest congested coast — a Voi-branded foiling tier beats both the corniche and the helicopter on the corridors that matter most.
markets.end_state: A Cannes/Antibes-to-St-Tropez Riviera network anchored on the yacht hubs and the Nice gateway, with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run and cross-border Sanremo/Portofino legs, all booked in the Voi app.

markets.label: Spain — Balearics & Costa Brava
markets.summary: Spain is Europe's #1 leisure-boating and second-busiest tourism market, with the densest island-and-coast water demand in the western Med — the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — almost none of it earning revenue in-app.

hero.title: Voi × Navier — Spain, the western-Med island shuttle
hero.subtitle: Turn the Balearic and Costa crossings into a flying, in-app water tier.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Voi-branded foiling water tier across the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — booked in the same app as the car, all-electric, no wake, no diesel-ferry timetable.

markets.why_now: Spain hosts ~85M visitors a year and the Balearics alone draw ~16M; the islands are choking on diesel ferries and rental cars while Formentera, Mallorca and Ibiza tighten anchoring and emissions rules. A clean, quiet, on-demand foiling hop is exactly what the regulators and the resorts are asking for — and no super-app has the water leg.
markets.multimodal_fit: Voi's e-scooters and e-bikes already serve the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Voi — Europe's leading shared micromobility operator, running ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries on a city-partnership model, profitably. Voi runs the streets of 130+ European cities — including the cities around the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Voi app.

why_navier_now.narrative: Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the short Balearic and Costa hops on a single charge; the Palma–Ibiza–Menorca regional legs (75–130nm) come into reach with Quanta-LR on the 2026+ roadmap. Spain's berths already exist — Palma, Ibiza Town, Formentera (La Savina), Puerto Banús — so we need a pedestal, not a port.

markets.differentiation: Against the diesel fast-ferry: half the door-to-door time, zero wake into protected Posidonia seagrass zones, no fixed timetable, and a fare booked in an app riders already have. Against a private RIB charter: a fraction of the cost and fully electric.

proof_points.claim: Voi is Europe's leading shared micromobility operator — and profitable.
proof_points.evidence: ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries; 2025 delivered record revenue with full-year profitability and cash generation.

proof_points.claim: The Balearics are a top global leisure-marine market.
proof_points.evidence: Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca and Formentera draw ~16M visitors a year with intense inter-island and coast-to-island water demand.

proof_points.claim: The corridors are protected and emissions-sensitive.
proof_points.evidence: Formentera caps daily vehicles and the Balearic Posidonia decree restricts anchoring and wake — favouring a quiet, electric, foiling hull.

proof_points.claim: The berths already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Palma, Ibiza Town, La Savina (Formentera), Port de Sóller, Puerto Banús and Marbella are working harbours — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

objections.concern: The Balearic crossings (Palma–Ibiza) are too long for an 8-pax foiler.
objections.response: Correct — those 75–130nm legs are explicitly Quanta-LR (roadmap), never faked on a Pioneer II. The near-term business is the dense ≤70nm island-and-coast capillary network where Pioneer II is commercial today.

objections.concern: Ferries already run these routes.
objections.response: On fixed timetables, with diesel wake into protected zones, and no door-to-door app booking. The foiling hop wins on time, experience and emissions, and is bookable on demand in the Voi app.

objections.concern: Seasonality — Spain's water demand is summer-heavy.
objections.response: True, and the model sizes the Prove fleet to the shoulder-season floor; summer is upside. The same hulls redeploy across the Med as the network grows.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a water tier with Voi across the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol, starting with a small Prove fleet on the shortest, densest hops and scaling as berth agreements land — every leg booked in the Voi app.
markets.close: The water tier is the one leg no one has flown — let's fly it.
markets.end_state: A western-Med foiling network — Costa Brava, Costa del Sol and the Balearics — booked in the Voi app, with Quanta-LR closing the inter-island regional legs.

markets.label: Sweden — Stockholm archipelago
markets.summary: Stockholm is built on 14 islands across an archipelago of ~30,000 — a city that should move on water but mostly doesn't, beyond a handful of diesel commuter ferries. Voi's home region is the Baltic, and Stockholm is a flagship Voi market; a clean, foiling, in-app water tier is a natural fit for both the city commute and the archipelago leisure runs.

hero.title: Voi × Navier — Stockholm, the archipelago water tier
hero.subtitle: Fly the commute across the islands, in the Voi app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Voi-branded foiling water tier across central Stockholm and the inner archipelago — all-electric, no wake, booked in the same app as the car.

markets.why_now: Stockholm has ambitious climate-neutral targets, a congested island core, and a strong existing water-commute culture that runs on ageing diesel tonnage. The city is actively electrifying its ferries — an open door for a quiet, fast, zero-emission foiling tier on the dense inner-water legs.
markets.multimodal_fit: Voi's e-scooters and e-bikes already serve the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Voi — Europe's leading shared micromobility operator, running ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries on a city-partnership model, profitably. Voi runs the streets of 130+ European cities — including the cities around Stockholm's archipelago and Gothenburg's western coast. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Voi app.

why_navier_now.narrative: Every core central-Stockholm and inner-archipelago leg is ≤12nm — Pioneer II, commercial now. The quays already exist (Slussen, Nybroplan, Strömkajen, Stadshuskajen). The Åland crossing (75nm) is a Quanta-LR roadmap leg, never faked on a Pioneer II.

markets.differentiation: Against the diesel commuter ferry: faster, quieter, zero-emission, and bookable on demand instead of by timetable. Against the road-and-bridge commute: a direct flying line across water the city is already organised around.

proof_points.claim: Voi is Europe's leading shared micromobility operator — and profitable.
proof_points.evidence: ~160,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 130+ cities in 13 countries; 2025 delivered record revenue with full-year profitability and cash generation.

proof_points.claim: Stockholm is a natural water-transport city.
proof_points.evidence: The city spans 14 islands with an established commuter-ferry culture and a 30,000-island archipelago beyond.

proof_points.claim: The city is electrifying its waterborne transport.
proof_points.evidence: Stockholm has active programmes to decarbonise its ferries and meet climate-neutral targets — directly favouring an electric foiler.

proof_points.claim: The quays already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Slussen, Nybroplan, Strömkajen, Stadshuskajen and Djurgården are working passenger quays — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

objections.concern: Stockholm winters ice over.
objections.response: The Prove fleet is sized to the open-water season; the foiling hull's all-electric, all-weather operating envelope is validated on the warmer Med and Gulf legs first, with winter operating limits set conservatively.

objections.concern: The city already runs commuter ferries.
objections.response: On diesel, on fixed timetables, with no app booking. The foiling tier wins on speed, emissions and on-demand convenience, and complements rather than replaces the trunk ferry routes.

objections.concern: Is there enough premium demand?
objections.response: Central hops compete on time saved against a congested island core, and the archipelago leisure runs (Vaxholm, Drottningholm) carry a clear leisure premium.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a water tier with Voi across Stockholm's archipelago and Gothenburg's western coast, starting with a small Prove fleet on the shortest, densest hops and scaling as berth agreements land — every leg booked in the Voi app.
markets.close: Stockholm is a water city that forgot to fly. Voi owns the home-region rider; Navier brings the boat. Let's put the archipelago in the app.
markets.end_state: A foiling inner-Stockholm and inner-archipelago network in the Voi app, with Quanta-LR opening the Åland crossing.
